contract.structural_score_basis: ⚠️ AUTHORED 2026-09-21 from riskAnalyst's own enumeration. This asset has no security_analyst authority walk and one was NOT commissioned; see coverage_note, which names what that leaves unestablished. ⚠️ THE LARGEST SINGLE DEDUCTION IS THE ONE-HOUR TIMELOCK, and it is worth stating plainly: DUSD's owner is an AltoTimelockController at 0xfAe841679dc1A93D225ECc827E4BbF3e8d703F86 whose minDelay() is 3,600 SECONDS. Nobody monitors a one-hour queue, so it is not a reaction window — it is a formality with the shape of one. It was 0 at construction and set to 3,600 at block 23,983,212, while the delay was still zero, so the change was self-executing. A 4-of-7 quorum does not offset the absence of notice. ⚠️ AND GOVERNANCE, TREASURY AND EMERGENCY PAUSE ARE THE SAME SEVEN KEYS: three distinct Safes (0xc49bf619cc9A68F84A6c9Ab88506f2627565a4D0 governance, 0xA1148A1b94262540994Cf9Aa431A13ad39764228 treasury, 0x1c11d2d42929bd17Ab7212b79c91862ADFa8bBE4 emergency) each return the IDENTICAL seven EOA owners at the identical 4-of-7 threshold, read individually rather than assumed. There is no separation of duties and the effective compromise threshold for the whole system is four keys. ✅ WHAT ARGUES UP, and it is substantial: the token contract is NOT A PROXY — EIP-1967 implementation, admin and beacon slots all read zero, 16,565 bytes of immutable bytecode, so there is no upgrade path for the token itself. It inherits LayerZero OFT but PeerSet has NEVER been emitted, so the cross-chain mint surface that makes setPeer unlimited-mint authority on comparable OFTs is inert today and DUSD is Ethereum-only. AltoTimelockController is hardened over stock OpenZeppelin: grantRole and revokeRole revert unless called by the timelock itself, forcing role changes through the queue, and renouncing the admin role is blocked. Every deployer EOA revoked its own proposer, executor, canceller and admin roles at block 23,989,753; no EOA holds any timelock role today. rescueTokens is correctly bounded to the balance in excess of _currentExposure or _accruedFees. ⚠️ WHAT FOUR SIGNATURES PLUS ONE HOUR CAN STILL DO: authorize an arbitrary minter at an arbitrary ceiling; upgrade the UUPS stability modules that hold the reserves; enable cross-chain minting via setPeer; and call Usm.seize(), which transfers the module's ENTIRE underlying — 722,605 frxUSD, 88% of all backing — to stableTokenTreasury while LEAVING THE DUSD OUTSTANDING, with burnAfterSeize an optional follow-up at the same role's discretion and the recipient being a Safe the same signers control. is_seized is therefore a solvency field, not a status flag. A free flash-mint of 500,000 DUSD (61% of supply, flashFee 0) also exists; Alto itself is insulated because its lending hardcodes DUSD at $1, so the exposure is any external integrator pricing DUSD from the pool. 5.0 rather than lower because the immutable token, the ten published audits and the revoked deployer roles are real; 5.0 rather than higher because one hour and four keys reach everything above.

contract.coverage_note: ⚠️ THE AUTHORITY HALF OF THIS AXIS IS NOT WALKED, AND THIS SCORE MUST NOT BE PRESENTED AS AN AUTHORITY WALK. What IS established is a full event-history ENUMERATION by riskAnalyst — not a match against an expected list: all 21 SetMinterStatus, 50 SetMinterCeiling and 21 SetBurnerStatus events (19 minters ever, 17 live); all 3 OwnershipTransferred; all 828 timelock events including every RoleGranted and RoleRevoked; the MinDelayChange history; the pauser set; and PeerSet returning zero rows. A negative control was run — 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD returns false on every timelock role — so the hasRole reads discriminate rather than being universally true. ⚠️ TWO NAMED GAPS REMAIN. FIRST: who can DRIVE the EmergencyController at 0x3c822f14a90955bf35278b42ba509feecad3a305 is NOT established. It holds pause rights on the token and SWAP_FREEZER_ROLE on the stability module, and its own authority was never walked — so the pause surface has a holder whose controller is unknown. SECOND: the seven signer identities are unresearched and no cross-protocol signer-overlap sweep was run, so whether these keys also control other assets we hold or assess is unknown. ⚠️ A methodological note that belongs with the enumeration: the pauser set was found only AFTER a first signature guess returned zero rows — Pausable emits PauserUpdated(address,bytes32,bool), not SetPauser — so an empty result was a false negative rather than an absence. Anyone extending this enumeration should enumerate rather than match.
